stem: Meena wants to find out whether the temperature of the oil affects how much a puri puffs up when fried. Which pair of trials is a fair test?

options.text: Trial 1: oil at 160 °C, puri 2 mm thick, dropped gently. Trial 2: oil at 180 °C, puri 4 mm thick, dropped from a height.
Trial 1: oil at 160 °C, puri 2 mm thick, dropped the same way. Trial 2: oil at 180 °C, puri 2 mm thick, dropped the same way.
Trial 1: oil at 160 °C, puri 2 mm thick. Trial 2: oil at 160 °C, puri 4 mm thick, both dropped the same way.
Trial 1: oil at 180 °C, puri 2 mm thick, dropped gently. Trial 2: oil at 180 °C, puri 2 mm thick, dropped from a height.

teacher.key_rationale: A fair test of oil temperature changes only the oil temperature while keeping puri thickness and dropping method identical; only option B does this. A changes thickness and dropping too, C keeps temperature the same and changes thickness (tests the wrong factor), D changes only the dropping method.
